reuse.why: The change reuses getScheduledAmount and getApproxNumberThreshold, although the budget template still conditionally bypasses the amount helper.

duplication.why: Existing midpoint implementations are consolidated, but the budget template retains operator dispatch and single-value passthrough already handled by getScheduledAmount.

placement.why: Schedule amount policy stays in shared/schedules.ts and reuses the tolerance definition in shared/rules.ts across server and desktop consumers.

scope.why: The edits are focused on schedule amount policy, its consumers, the requested API field, and supporting tests and release notes.

maintainability.why: Centralization substantially improves ownership, but redundant budget dispatch and comments and release notes describing superseded policy leave avoidable maintenance friction.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/schedule-template.ts:createScheduleList calls getScheduledAmount only for isbetween and isapprox, handling other values locally.

disguised_duplication.where: createScheduleList reshapes amount dispatch into an operator-based conditional while retaining the single-value passthrough that getScheduledAmount already provides.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount adds the necessary op parameter and isapprox branch; createScheduleList retains a partial bypass through its local operator dispatch.
